newsitem.title: UK: British royal yacht Britannia on final voyage.
newsitem.headline: British royal yacht Britannia on final voyage.

text.p: The royal yacht Britannia, symbol of the days when Britain ruled the waves, left on Monday on its final voyage to mark the sun setting on British rule in Hong Kong.
The sleek 6,000-tonne, luxurious mini-liner that costs about 10 million pounds ($17 million) a year to run, is being taken out of service after 44 years afloat.

Heir to the throne Prince Charles, who as a child holidayed aboard Britannia and also used it on his honeymoon with Princess Diana, will sail out of Hong Kong a few minutes after midnight on July 1, when the colony is handed back to China.
The yacht, with a crew of 234 and a Royal Marines band on board, will call first at Malta and then stop off in the Gulf and countries in Asia before its visit to Hong Kong.
Charles, whose marriage to Diana ended in divorce last year, will use it as a base for official visits to the Gulf states of Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar.
British exporters say the vessel is a unique asset that more than paid its way by helping to secure two billion pounds ($3.35 billion) of exports for Britain over the past decade.
"It is able to attract a very high quality trade audience. When the royal yacht sits in a harbour, people want to come aboard," said Andrew Buxton, chairman of banking giant Barclays.
But ministers, fearing a taxpayers' backlash as the popularity of the royal family slides, are reluctant to decide before an imminent general election whether to replace Britannia.
"It is a decision the government has to make. It is not an easy decision," junior defence minister Nicholas Soames told reporters.
"I am in no doubt myself, not only from personal experience but all that one sees and hears, of the immense benefit of a royal yacht. No decision has yet been made."

Britannia will visit 17 countries before returning to Britain early in August, when for the last time she will take Queen Elizabeth and her family on their traditional summer cruise around the Western Isles of Scotland.

All proponents of replacements for Britannia, ranging from a royal sail training ship to a combined royal yacht and cruise ship, have stressed that it would be built in Britain and demonstrate British marine expertise.
